Is "Valve Train" an industry standard term?  When I search on Google I don't see any hits outside of internal combustion engines.
Changed this to Valve instead now, hence marking this as resolved.
So there would be another Valve interface on D-Bus with this name?  If so, would an association work better?

> So there would be another Valve interface on D-Bus with this name?  

The name would be different but this property tells whats the name of the other item in the pair. For example, 
Name: SupplyValve1 is paired with ReturnValve1 by using this decorator. The pair decorator for one needs to have other one's in its value. So, the consumer can lookup this name for that inventory item type and figure out whats it is paired with.

> If so, would an association work better?

First i had thought about associations too. Can entity manager create associations based on name between 2 such items?

It kinda sounds like EM's 'physical topology' associations, which creates associations between its own objects.  It would take some invention to figure out how to get the code to do that for this case, so this way would certainly be easier.  I'm sure @patrick@stwcx.xyz will have an opinion here so I'll defer to him.
Can thsi just be an enum?

Right now i have made this as enum in EM schema https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77415/13/schemas/openbmc-dbus.json and made it string here because defining as enum in PDI will prepend it with xyz.openbmc_project.X and i was asked to not use xyz.openbmc_project.X enum values in EM schemas.
Makes sense to me.

Arbitrary strings are not allowed.  I'm tired of deficiencies in entity-manager being used as reasons here.  There are already tons of "xyz.openbmc_project" in entity-manager configs.  This is an enum; make it an enum.  Fix entity-manager.

Sure, i have changed this to enum here and changed it to string in EM as in other inventory items.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/83404
The related EM patch for this change has been merged https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77415.
If we have the pairing, why do we need this?  Can you be clearer what the purpose of this is.  I don't know why we need a "pair name".

There is no pairing as such, as Supply and Return valves are 2 different inventory items. The only thing which can make them a pair is this PairName property. Initially i had created a pair decorator but in one of our discussions you had mentioned that it will create a general use for that decorator outside of Valve as well, hence i dropped that idea and just added this PairName property.

I have updated the description for property to add more details on the purpose. Marking this as resolved for now, please let me know if there are any further questions on this.

But you have the association already... I'm not following why we need an arbitrary string name.

With a property, you can't "find the other end of the pair" anyhow without looking at every single instance.  Generally that's fairly bad for performance... so what are you trying to accomplish with this?  I'm not understanding what daemon is the consumer.

EM doesn't support creating associations like this. This definition is for inventory item which gets exposed from EM. The reactor would need to create the association by looking at the PairName value, just like other associations which gets created from reactors.
Information which originates from entity-manager for consumption by other processes should be in the Configuration space, right?  The PairName sounds like a new Configuration object then.

> Information which originates from entity-manager for consumption by other processes should be in the Configuration space, right?  The PairName sounds like a new Configuration object then.

I was also intending to use the PairName as CoolantLoop Name in the Redfish https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/schema/dmtf/json-schema/CoolantConnector.v1_2_0.json#L88 as that seems more of an inventory data instead.

I gave this one a second thought and i think you are right and its better if we have this as part of configuration. The CoolantLoop by itself will be an inventory object to which Valves can connect. So, having pairName/LoopName in Valve configuration will be better. I have dropped PairName from valve inventory item.
No.  Set it to an empty string.  Arbitary values that hold meaning are not something that should be documented in the description of a dbus interface.
Done
Add default Unknown please.
Done

Disclaimer: never did anything with liquid cooling

IMO Valves and pipes can form a directed graph for liquid flow, right?

My main concern, how do we communicate this.

If there is a valve A, then a distribution block, then 3 valves {B,C,D},
then a return valve E,
how do we configure these connections with associations?

```
A (supply) --> block
               | | |
               B C D
               | | |
E (return) <-- block
```


What do you think about having `connecting`/ `connected_with` association to configure this.

Maybe we can have a boolean for `isSupplyValve` and `isReturnValve`, to mark supply and return valves for the whole system.

Then by walking the graph between those 2 one could figure out which supply can be paired with which return.

If we name the association `paired_with`, it sounds to me like there are only 2 valves (because of the word `pair`).

Sorry, I had missed dropping the pairing association from my last patch as i don't need this anymore.

There is one return and supply valve for a coolant loop, thats how the Redfish spec defines it and thats how i have seen the liquid cooling loops in general. I would be implementing a CoolantLoop inventory item which will have Supply and Return valves as its two ends. And yes, for that i am going to use the connected_to/connecting association as that makes sense.
